explanation.why: Cognito provides identity management for applications and does not scan EC2 instances.

questions.question: A company needs to track the activity in its AWS accounts, and needs to know when an API call is made against its AWS resources. Which AWS tool or service can be used to meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs but does not record API call history by default.
explanation.why: CloudWatch focuses on performance metrics and application logs. API call auditing requires a different service.

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not API activity.
explanation.why: Inspector evaluates EC2 instances and container images for security issues but does not track API calls.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudTrail records API calls made against AWS resources.
keyPoints: Tracks who did what and when
examples: Identifying who terminated an EC2 instance
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS CloudTrail provides event history of AWS account activity, including API calls made through the console, CLI, SDKs, and other AWS services. It is the primary service for governance, compliance, and security auditing and is heavily tested in AWS exams.

explanation.summary: AWS IAM manages identities and permissions, not activity logging.
explanation.why: IAM controls access but does not log API activity. CloudTrail performs that function.

questions.question: A company wants a fully managed Windows file server for its Windows-based applications. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: Amazon FSx provides a fully managed Windows file server.
examples: Hosting shared file storage for Windows applications
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is specifically designed to support Windows-based workloads. It provides a fully managed file system with native SMB support and Active Directory integration. Exams commonly test FSx when Windows file servers are mentioned.

explanation.summary: Amazon EKS is a container orchestration service.
explanation.why: EKS manages Kubernetes clusters and does not provide Windows file server functionality.

explanation.summary: Amazon ECS runs containerized applications.
explanation.why: ECS orchestrates containers and does not provide managed file server storage.

explanation.summary: Amazon EMR is used for big data processing.
explanation.why: EMR runs analytics frameworks and does not offer Windows file server capabilities.

questions.question: A developer has been hired by a large company and needs AWS credentials. Which are security best practices that should be followed? (Choose two.)

options.text: Grant the developer access to only the AWS resources needed to perform the job.

explanation.summary: Applying the principle of least privilege limits security risk.
examples: Granting read-only access to S3 buckets
Limiting EC2 permissions to specific instances
explanation.additionalInfo: The principle of least privilege is a core AWS security best practice. Developers should only be granted the permissions required to perform their tasks. This approach minimizes risk and is heavily tested in AWS certification exams.

options.text: Share the AWS account root user credentials with the developer.

explanation.summary: Sharing root credentials is a severe security risk.
explanation.why: The root user has unrestricted access and should never be shared. Best practice is to protect the root account and use IAM users or roles instead.

options.text: Add the developer to the administrator’s group in AWS IAM.

explanation.summary: Granting administrator access violates least privilege.
explanation.why: Administrator permissions provide full access and should be limited to trusted admins only.

options.text: Configure a password policy that ensures the developer’s password cannot be changed.

explanation.summary: Passwords should be changeable and rotated periodically.
explanation.why: Preventing password changes increases security risk and conflicts with best practices.

options.text: Ensure the account password policy requires a minimum length.

explanation.summary: Strong password policies improve account security.
explanation.additionalInfo: Configuring strong password policies is a fundamental IAM security best practice. AWS exams frequently test password policy requirements alongside least privilege principles.

questions.question: Which tasks are the customer’s responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for the global infrastructure.
explanation.why: AWS designs, builds, and maintains Regions, Availability Zones, and data centers.

explanation.summary: Customers control encryption of their data.
examples: Encrypting files before uploading to S3
explanation.additionalInfo: Client-side encryption ensures that data is protected before it is sent to AWS. Under the shared responsibility model, customers decide when and how to encrypt their data. This concept is commonly tested in exams.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for managing IAM users, roles, and credentials.
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM configuration is a core customer responsibility. AWS provides the IAM service, but customers must manage identities and permissions. Exams frequently test IAM ownership under the shared responsibility model.

explanation.summary: AWS secures edge locations.
explanation.why: Edge locations are part of AWS global infrastructure and are secured by AWS.

explanation.summary: AWS manages patching for managed database services.
explanation.why: For Amazon RDS, AWS handles OS and database engine patching as part of the managed service.

questions.question: A company is running a workload in the AWS Cloud. Which AWS best practice ensures the MOST cost-effective architecture for the workload?

explanation.summary: Loose coupling improves resilience and scalability, not cost efficiency directly.
explanation.why: While beneficial for architecture, loose coupling does not inherently reduce costs.

explanation.summary: Rightsizing ensures resources match workload requirements.
explanation.additionalInfo: Rightsizing is a key AWS cost optimization best practice. By matching resource capacity to actual workload needs, organizations can significantly reduce cloud spend. Exams frequently test rightsizing in cost-focused scenarios.

explanation.summary: Caching improves performance and scalability but not overall cost efficiency alone.
explanation.why: Caching may reduce load but does not guarantee optimal cost without proper sizing.

explanation.summary: Redundancy improves availability but increases cost.
explanation.why: Running duplicate resources enhances resilience but does not optimize for cost.

questions.question: A company wants to automate infrastructure deployment by using infrastructure as code (IaC). The company wants to scale production stacks so the stacks can be deployed in multiple AWS Regions. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service.
explanation.why: CloudWatch collects metrics, logs, and events but does not deploy or manage infrastructure stacks.

explanation.summary: AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes.
explanation.why: Config provides compliance and auditing but does not deploy infrastructure across Regions.

explanation.summary: AWS Trusted Advisor provides best practice recommendations.
explanation.why: Trusted Advisor analyzes environments but does not automate infrastructure deployment.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudFormation enables infrastructure as code and multi-Region stack deployment.
examples: Deploying identical VPCs in multiple Regions
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS CloudFormation allows customers to define AWS resources using code and deploy them consistently. With StackSets, CloudFormation supports deploying stacks across multiple Regions and accounts. This is a common exam topic for IaC and multi-Region deployment scenarios.

questions.question: A company wants to grant users in one AWS account access to resources in another AWS account. The users do not currently have permission to access the resources. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: IAM groups manage permissions within a single AWS account.
explanation.why: Groups cannot grant cross-account access. They only organize users inside the same account.

explanation.summary: IAM roles enable secure cross-account access.
examples: Allowing Account A users to access S3 in Account B
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM roles are the recommended way to grant cross-account access in AWS. By defining a trust relationship, users in one account can assume a role in another account without sharing credentials. Exams frequently test IAM roles for cross-account access scenarios.

explanation.summary: IAM tags are used for attribute-based access control.
explanation.why: Tags help refine permissions but do not grant cross-account access by themselves.

explanation.summary: IAM Access Analyzer identifies unintended access.
explanation.why: It analyzes policies but does not grant or manage permissions.

questions.question: How does AWS Cloud computing help businesses reduce costs? (Choose two.)

options.text: AWS charges the same prices for services in every AWS Region.

explanation.summary: AWS pricing varies by Region.
explanation.why: Service prices differ across Regions due to operational and infrastructure costs.

options.text: AWS enables capacity to be adjusted on demand.

explanation.summary: On-demand scaling eliminates paying for unused resources.
keyPoints: Pay only for what you use
examples: Scaling EC2 instances during peak traffic
explanation.additionalInfo: Elasticity allows businesses to adjust capacity based on demand, eliminating the need to maintain excess infrastructure. This is a foundational AWS cost-saving benefit and is frequently tested in certification exams.

options.text: AWS offers discounts for Amazon EC2 instances that remain idle for more than 1 week.

explanation.summary: AWS does not provide discounts for idle instances.
explanation.why: Idle resources still incur charges unless they are stopped or terminated.

options.text: AWS does not charge for data sent from the AWS Cloud to the internet.

explanation.summary: AWS charges for most outbound data transfer.
explanation.why: Outbound data transfer to the internet typically incurs costs.

options.text: AWS eliminates many of the costs of building and maintaining on-premises data centers.

explanation.summary: AWS removes capital and operational expenses of on-premises infrastructure.
examples: No data center cooling or power costs
explanation.additionalInfo: By moving to AWS, organizations avoid the cost of building and operating physical data centers. This shift from CapEx to OpEx is a core AWS value proposition and a frequent exam topic.
